name: Combined Heat and Power Plant
use: Central cogeneration plant with chilled-water plant; primary heat and electricity source for the Durham campus
builtText: Cogeneration plant online 2006 on the existing central heating plant site (older plant date unknown)

renovations.what: Began burning processed landfill gas piped 12.7 miles from Rochester (EcoLine) as primary fuel

Utility distribution relocated: 800+ trench feet of steam, condensate and dual-temperature piping replacing a deteriorated tunnel section outside the plant (RMF Engineering, Charters Brothers); live late Nov 2022

facts.text: The cogeneration plant went online in 2006 as the primary source of heat and electricity for the five-million-square-foot Durham campus; with its chilled-water plant it cost about $28 million, self-financed.

Since 2009 its primary fuel is purified landfill methane from Waste Management's Rochester landfill; UNH says it was the first US university to use landfill gas as its primary fuel, for up to 85% of campus energy.
The plant shares a College Road site with the 1939 Service Building and its smokestack.
A 2020 condition assessment found deteriorating utility tunnels; a relocated section of the campus loop outside the plant went live in late 2022 and won an ABC Excellence in Construction award.

s4l.title: Enabling the Future of the Campus Experience (2023-11)

verdict: Industrial cogeneration plant that runs the campus on landfill gas, a genuine first; nothing to look at.
notes: No photo of the plant itself; the only reference is the archives Service Building shot with the smokestack. The year of the 2022 utility work is inferred from "fall of 2022 heating season" and "late November of last year" in a Nov 2023 article. The EcoLine page is older and its forward-looking claims (e.g. 85%) may be dated. Old row said "older heating plant on site, date unknown": still unknown.
